PDF：TCP1.4-2026年最新版本.pdf
This is the core textbook for the TCP knowledge base. Use it as the main learning path: understand the structure first, then extract rules, calculations, examples, and mistake cards by module.
中文提示：笔记正文尽量保留英文税法术语，中文只写“易错提醒”和自己的理解。
Textbook Role

Subject: TCP / Tax Compliance and Planning
Purpose: core reading source, module structure, rule source, example source
Workflow: follow TCP Textbook Map

Major Units

TCP 1 - Individuals
TCP 2 - Corporations
TCP 3 - Flow-Through and Other Entities
TCP 4 - Dispositions and Related Party Transactions

H.A.R.N.E.S.S. Workflow
H - Highlight
Only highlight:

formulas
limitations and phase-outs
exceptions
confusing comparisons
example-solving steps

A - Ask
For each subsection, ask at least one exam-style question:

When does this rule apply?
What are the exceptions?
What numerical threshold matters?
How could an exam question hide the key condition?

R - Rephrase
Rewrite textbook language into clear rule statements:

If X occurs, Y is generally required.
Z is allowed only when A, B, and C are satisfied.
The key is not calculation first; it is eligibility first.

N - Network
Each important rule should link to:

one topic: 美国税法 TCP
one module
one example or mistake card

E - Extract
Extract three types of cards:

Rule card: definition, conditions, exceptions
Calculation card: formula, steps, numerical thresholds
Comparison card: differences between similar concepts

S - Synthesize
After each module, write a one-page module summary:

what the module is about
high-frequency rules
high-frequency numbers
common traps
typical question patterns

S - Ship
Each week, create one learning output:

one-page cheat sheet
Anki-style question set
mistake review
topic summary

04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---consolidated-.title: 2026 Update Card - Consolidated Taxable Income
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---consolidated-.content:
2026 Update - Consolidated Taxable Income
Calculation Steps

Calculate each member’s stand-alone taxable income.
Remove intercompany transaction effects.
Remove items determined at the consolidated level.
Combine member taxable incomes.
Apply consolidated-level items.

Consolidated-Level Items

Capital gains and losses
Section 1231 gains and losses
NOL
Charitable contribution deduction
DRD

Chinese Note

易错提醒：intercompany items are removed before consolidated-level items are applied.

04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---ira-and-rmd-r.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/2026 Update Card - IRA and RMD Rules.md
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---ira-and-rmd-r.title: 2026 Update Card - IRA and RMD Rules
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---ira-and-rmd-r.content:
2026 Update - IRA and RMD Rules
IRA Contribution Limits

Under age 50: $7,500
Age 50 or older: $8,600

RMD Age
Traditional 401(k) RMDs begin by April 1 of the year after the later of reaching:

age 73, if born between 1951 and 1959;
age 75, if born in 1960 or later; or
terminating employment with the plan sponsor.

RMD Penalty

25%
reduced to 10% if corrected timely

Chinese Note

易错提醒：Roth 401(k) is not subject to these RMD requirements.

04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---section-1202-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/2026 Update Card - Section 1202 QSBS.md
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---section-1202-.title: 2026 Update Card - Section 1202 QSBS
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---section-1202-.content:
2026 Update - Section 1202 QSBS
Aggregate Gross Assets Limit

Stock issued on or before July 4, 2025: $50 million
Stock issued after July 4, 2025: $75 million

Maximum Exclusion Per Shareholder

Stock acquired on or before July 4, 2025: greater of 10 times basis or 10 million (5 million if MFS)
Stock acquired after July 4, 2025: greater of 10 times basis or 15 million (7.5 million if MFS) for 2026

Chinese Note

易错提醒：QSBS 现在必须看 acquisition/issuance date around July 4, 2025.

04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---standard-dedu.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/2026 Update Card - Standard Deduction and Itemized Deduction Changes.md
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---standard-dedu.title: 2026 Update Card - Standard Deduction and Itemized Deduction Changes
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---standard-dedu.content:
2026 Update - Standard Deduction and Itemized Deduction Changes
2026 Standard Deduction

Single: $16,100
Head of household: $24,150
MFJ or surviving spouse: $32,200
MFS: $16,100

Key Itemized Deduction Updates

SALT limit: $40,400 in 2026.
Cash charitable deduction for nonitemizers: 1,000, or 2,000 MFJ.
Charitable contributions: 0.5% of AGI floor.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：旧卡片中的 2023 standard deduction 数字只用于旧例题；2026 复习看本卡。

04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---trump-account.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/2026 Update Card - Trump Accounts.md
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---trump-account.title: 2026 Update Card - Trump Accounts
04-卡片笔记/2026-update-card---trump-account.content:
2026 Update - Trump Accounts
Core Rule
Trump accounts are tax-deferred investment accounts for children under age 18 with a valid Social Security number.
Key Limits

Available starting July 4, 2026.
Pilot federal contribution: $1,000 for qualifying U.S. citizen children born January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2028.
Employer contribution limit: $2,500 per year.
Maximum total contribution: $5,000 per year.
No deduction for contributions.
No distributions before the calendar year the beneficiary turns 18.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：Trump account is treated like a traditional IRA after age 18, but has special child-account restrictions before then.

04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---amti-basic-fo.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Calculation Card - AMTI Basic Formula.md
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---amti-basic-fo.title: Calculation Card - AMTI Basic Formula
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---amti-basic-fo.content:
AMTI Basic Formula
Core Formula
Regular taxable income

AMT adjustments
AMT preference items
= Alternative minimum taxable income (AMTI)

Adjustments
Adjustments exist because AMT rules treat certain income or deduction items differently from regular tax rules. Some are timing differences, while others permanently disallow certain regular tax benefits for AMT purposes.
Preference Items
Preference items increase AMTI. They are generally tax benefits allowed for regular tax but not allowed for AMT.
Exam Approach

Start with regular taxable income.
Identify AMT adjustments.
Identify AMT preference items.
Add them to compute AMTI.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：AMTI 不是从 gross income 重新开始算，而是从 regular taxable income 开始调整。

04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---after-tax-ret.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Calculation Card - After-Tax Return on Investment.md
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---after-tax-ret.title: Calculation Card - After-Tax Return on Investment
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---after-tax-ret.content:
After-Tax Return on Investment
ROI Formula
ROI = (Investment sales price - Cost of investment) / Cost of investment
After-Tax Rate of Return
After-tax return adjusts the investment return for taxes.
Exam Approach

Compute pre-tax return.
Identify the applicable tax rate.
Reduce the return by the tax effect.
Compare investments on an after-tax basis.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：投资回报不能只看 pre-tax ROI，税率会改变真正收益。

04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---charitable-co.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Calculation Card - Charitable Contribution AGI Limits.md
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---charitable-co.title: Calculation Card - Charitable Contribution AGI Limits
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---charitable-co.content:
Charitable Contribution AGI Limits
Core Limits

Cash contributions to public charities: generally 60% of AGI.
Ordinary income property: generally 50% of AGI.
Long-term capital gain property: generally 30% of AGI.

Carryforward
Excess charitable contributions may be carried forward for five years.
Exam Approach

Classify the contribution.
Determine the deductible amount before AGI limits.
Apply the correct AGI limitation.
Track any carryforward.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：先决定 property type，再决定 AGI limit。顺序不要反。

04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---excess-busine.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Calculation Card - Excess Business Loss Limitation.md
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---excess-busine.title: Calculation Card - Excess Business Loss Limitation
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---excess-busine.content:
Excess Business Loss Limitation
Core Rule
Taxpayers cannot deduct an overall excess business loss for the year. The limitation applies after the passive activity loss rules.
2023 Thresholds

Married filing jointly: $578,000.
All other taxpayers: $289,000.

Carryforward
The excess business loss is carried forward as a net operating loss (NOL).
Exam Approach

Apply tax basis, at-risk, and PAL limitations first.
Combine business income and business losses.
Apply the threshold amount.
Carry forward the excess as an NOL.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：excess business loss 是最后一道门槛，不能放在 PAL 前面。

04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---timing-of-inc.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Calculation Card - Timing of Income and Deductions.md
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---timing-of-inc.title: Calculation Card - Timing of Income and Deductions
04-卡片笔记/calculation-card---timing-of-inc.content:
Timing of Income and Deductions
Core Rule
Tax planning often compares whether income or deductions should be accelerated or deferred. The best answer depends on tax rates and the time value of money.
Income Timing

Deferring income is generally beneficial when tax rates are constant because tax is paid later.
Accelerating income may be beneficial if the current tax rate is lower than the future tax rate.

Deduction Timing

Accelerating deductions is generally beneficial when tax rates are constant because tax savings arrive earlier.
Deferring deductions may be beneficial if the future tax rate is meaningfully higher.

Calculation Pattern

Compute tax cost or tax savings.
Apply the present value factor if the tax effect occurs in a future year.
Compare after-tax income or after-tax cost.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：收入和扣除方向相反。收入通常想延后，扣除通常想提前，但税率变化可能改变答案。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---c-corporation-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - C Corporation vs Flow-Through Entities.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---c-corporation-.title: Comparison Card - C Corporation vs Flow-Through Entities
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---c-corporation-.content:
C Corporation vs Flow-Through Entities
C Corporation

Entity-level tax applies.
Shareholder-level tax may apply when earnings are distributed as dividends.
Certain fringe benefits may be more favorable.

Flow-Through Entities

Income and losses generally pass through to owners.
Individual owners may qualify for the 20% QBI deduction.
Losses may be limited by basis, at-risk, passive activity, and excess business loss rules.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：C corp 的关键词是 double taxation；flow-through 的关键词是 pass-through and owner-level limitations。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---charitable-don.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Charitable Donations of Noncash Property.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---charitable-don.title: Comparison Card - Charitable Donations of Noncash Property
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---charitable-don.content:
Charitable Donations of Noncash Property
Ordinary Income Property
Deduction is generally the lesser of adjusted basis or FMV.
Examples include:

inventory
short-term assets
depreciated investment or personal-use property
depreciation recapture portion of business-use property

Long-Term Capital Gain Property
Deduction is generally FMV if the property is appreciated capital gain property held for more than one year.
Tangible Personal Property - Unrelated Use
If tangible personal property is used by the charity for an unrelated purpose, the deduction may be limited to adjusted basis.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：不是所有捐赠都按 FMV 扣。先判断 ordinary income property 还是 LTCG property。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---fsa-vs-hsa.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - FSA vs HSA.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---fsa-vs-hsa.title: Comparison Card - FSA vs HSA
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---fsa-vs-hsa.content:
FSA vs HSA
Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

Funded through salary reduction.
Used for qualified medical or dependent care expenses.
Generally subject to use-it-or-lose-it rules.
Unused amounts may be forfeited unless limited carryover or grace-period rules apply.

Health Savings Account (HSA)

Used with a high-deductible health plan.
Contributions can be made on a pre-tax basis.
Funds can accumulate if not spent.
Qualified medical withdrawals are tax-favored.

2023 HSA Limits

Individual: $3,850.
Family: $7,750.
Additional amount for age 55 or older: $1,000.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：FSA 更像年度预算，HSA 更像可以积累的税优账户。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---investment-ris.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Investment Risk Types.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---investment-ris.title: Comparison Card - Investment Risk Types
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---investment-ris.content:
Investment Risk Types
Nonsystematic Risk
Risk unique to a company or industry. It can generally be reduced through diversification.
Systematic Risk
Market-wide risk that affects the overall market. It cannot be eliminated through diversification.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：diversification 主要降低 nonsystematic risk，不消除 systematic risk。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---operating-vs-l.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Operating vs Liquidating Distributions.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---operating-vs-l.title: Comparison Card - Operating vs Liquidating Distributions
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---operating-vs-l.content:
Operating vs Liquidating Distributions
Operating Distributions
Operating distributions occur while the entity continues to exist. Tax treatment depends on entity type, E&P, basis, and property distributed.
Liquidating Distributions
Liquidating distributions occur when the owner or entity interest is being terminated. They often require final gain/loss and basis analysis.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：distribution 题先判断 operating 还是 liquidating，再判断 entity type。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---owner-compensa.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Owner Compensation by Entity Type.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---owner-compensa.title: Comparison Card - Owner Compensation by Entity Type
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---owner-compensa.content:
Owner Compensation by Entity Type
C and S Corporations
Shareholder-employees may receive salaries. Compensation must generally be reasonable.
Partnerships
Partners may receive guaranteed payments rather than employee wages.
Sole Proprietorships
The owner generally does not receive wages from the sole proprietorship.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：owner 拿钱的形式取决于 entity type，salary、guaranteed payment、distribution 不要混。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---simple-trust-v.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Simple Trust vs Complex Trust.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---simple-trust-v.title: Comparison Card - Simple Trust vs Complex Trust
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---simple-trust-v.content:
Simple Trust vs Complex Trust
Simple Trust
A simple trust must distribute all income annually, cannot distribute corpus, and cannot make charitable contributions.
Complex Trust
A complex trust is a non-grantor trust that does not meet the simple trust requirements.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：simple trust 三个条件都要满足。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---standard-deduc.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Standard Deduction vs Itemized Deduction.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---standard-deduc.title: Comparison Card - Standard Deduction vs Itemized Deduction
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---standard-deduc.content:
Standard Deduction vs Itemized Deduction
Core Rule
Taxpayers generally choose the larger benefit between the standard deduction and allowable itemized deductions.
2023 Standard Deduction Amounts

Single: $13,850.
Head of household: $20,800.
Married filing jointly or surviving spouse: $27,700.
Married filing separately: $13,850, if allowed.

Itemized Deduction Indicators
Itemizing may help when the taxpayer has large qualified expenses, such as:

charitable contributions
uninsured medical and dental expenses
mortgage interest and property taxes
significant casualty or theft losses

Bunching Strategy
When itemized deductions are close to the standard deduction, the taxpayer may bunch deductible payments into one year to exceed the standard deduction in that year.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：itemized deductions 不是有就一定有用，必须和 standard deduction 比较。

04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---traditional-vs.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Comparison Card - Traditional vs Roth Retirement Accounts.md
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---traditional-vs.title: Comparison Card - Traditional vs Roth Retirement Accounts
04-卡片笔记/comparison-card---traditional-vs.content:
Traditional vs Roth Retirement Accounts
Traditional

Contributions may be deductible or made pre-tax.
Earnings grow tax-deferred.
Distributions are generally taxable as ordinary income to the extent they represent deductible contributions and earnings.

Roth

Contributions are made after tax.
Qualified distributions can be tax-free.
Roth treatment is most valuable when future tax rates are expected to be higher.

Exam Approach

Identify the account type.
Determine contribution tax treatment.
Determine whether the distribution is qualified.
Separate principal and earnings if needed.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：Traditional 是 “tax benefit now”；Roth 是 “tax benefit later”。

04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-income.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Planning Card - Corporate Income Shifting.md
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-income.title: Planning Card - Corporate Income Shifting
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-income.content:
Corporate Income Shifting
Core Idea
Income-shifting strategies decide who or where should recognize income. They may involve jurisdictions, related parties, owner compensation, transfer pricing, or entity choice.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：income shifting 一定要考虑 arm’s-length、reasonable compensation 和 business purpose。

04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-timing.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Planning Card - Corporate Timing Strategies.md
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-timing.title: Planning Card - Corporate Timing Strategies
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---corporate-timing.content:
Corporate Timing Strategies
Core Idea
Timing strategies decide when income, deductions, NOLs, or capital losses should be recognized or used. The answer depends on tax rates, present value, carryovers, and business constraints.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：timing strategy 要看 tax rate changes 和 present value，不是机械地 defer income。

04-卡片笔记/planning-card---year-end-tax-pla.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Planning Card - Year-End Tax Planning.md
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---year-end-tax-pla.title: Planning Card - Year-End Tax Planning
04-卡片笔记/planning-card---year-end-tax-pla.content:
Year-End Tax Planning
Core Idea
Year-end tax planning often combines timing, deductions, withholding, retirement or health contributions, and capital gain planning to reduce tax or avoid penalties.
Common Planning Moves

Defer income when future tax cost is lower in present value.
Accelerate deductions when current-year tax savings are more valuable.
Bunch itemized deductions to exceed the standard deduction.
Contribute to tax-favored accounts when eligible.
Review withholding and estimated payments before year end.
Consider capital gain timing and holding period.

Exam Approach

Compute the baseline tax result.
Apply the planning move.
Recompute taxable income, tax, and payments.
Check penalties or safe harbors.
Compare after-tax outcomes.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：year-end planning 题通常是综合题，别只算 tax liability，也要看 withholding、safe harbor 和 penalty。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---beat-and-fdii-overvi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - BEAT and FDII Overview.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---beat-and-fdii-overvi.title: Rule Card - BEAT and FDII Overview
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---beat-and-fdii-overvi.content:
BEAT and FDII Overview
BEAT
BEAT is a minimum tax aimed at large U.S. corporations with significant deductible payments to related foreign affiliates.
FDII
FDII provides a deduction for certain foreign-derived intangible income earned by U.S. C corporations.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：BEAT is defensive anti-base-erosion; FDII is incentive-style export/intangible treatment.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-a.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Below-Market Loans and Imputed Interest.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-a.title: Rule Card - Below-Market Loans and Imputed Interest
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-a.content:
Below-Market Loans and Imputed Interest
Core Rule
When a loan charges no interest or interest below the applicable federal rate, tax law may impute interest. The foregone interest is treated as if it had been paid and then transferred back between the parties.
Loans Commonly Tested

Gift loans
Compensation-related loans
Corporation-shareholder loans
Tax-avoidance loans
Certain loans involving qualified continuing care facilities

Exam Approach

Identify the relationship between lender and borrower.
Determine whether the loan is below-market.
Check whether an exception applies.
Calculate or identify foregone interest.
Determine the income, deduction, compensation, dividend, or gift consequence.

High-Yield Exceptions

Certain loans of $10,000 or less may qualify for a de minimis exception.
Gift loans of $100,000 or less may have a limitation based on the borrower’s net investment income.
Exceptions do not apply when tax avoidance is a main purpose.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：below-market loan 的重点不是“有没有真的付利息”，而是税法是否把利息视同发生。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-i.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Below-Market Loans in Related Party Transactions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-i.title: Rule Card - Below-Market Loans in Related Party Transactions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---below-market-loans-i.content:
Below-Market Loans in Related Party Transactions
Core Rule
Section 7872 can recharacterize a below-market loan as an arm’s-length loan with imputed interest, causing tax consequences to both lender and borrower.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：below-market loan 的税务结果是“视同有 interest”，不是只看实际付款。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---boot-and-liabilities.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Boot and Liabilities in Corporate Formation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---boot-and-liabilities.title: Rule Card - Boot and Liabilities in Corporate Formation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---boot-and-liabilities.content:
Boot and Liabilities in Corporate Formation
Core Rule
Boot received in a Section 351 transaction can trigger recognized gain. Liabilities assumed by the corporation can also trigger gain when liabilities exceed the adjusted basis of transferred assets.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：recognized gain is limited, but liabilities in excess of basis can still create gain.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---charitable-contribut.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Charitable Contribution Substantiation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---charitable-contribut.title: Rule Card - Charitable Contribution Substantiation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---charitable-contribut.content:
Charitable Contribution Substantiation
Core Rule
Noncash charitable contributions may require additional documentation.
Key Requirements

More than $500 of noncash property: file Form 8283.
More than $5,000 for one item or group of similar items: generally obtain a written qualified appraisal.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：大额 noncash donation 不只是算 deduction，还要满足 substantiation。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---complete-vs-incomple.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Complete vs Incomplete Gifts.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---complete-vs-incomple.title: Rule Card - Complete vs Incomplete Gifts
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---complete-vs-incomple.content:
Complete vs Incomplete Gifts
Core Rule
Only complete gifts are subject to gift tax and eligible for the annual gift tax exclusion.
Complete Gift
A gift is complete when the donor has given up sufficient control over the property.
Incomplete Gift
A gift is incomplete if the donor retains meaningful power to revoke, alter, or control the transfer.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：gift tax 不只是问“有没有送”，还要问 donor 是否真的放弃控制。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Consolidated Return Affiliated Group.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.title: Rule Card - Consolidated Return Affiliated Group
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.content:
Consolidated Return Affiliated Group
Core Rule
An affiliated group may file a consolidated return when the parent meets the ownership requirements and all members are eligible and consent.
Ownership Test
The parent generally must own at least 80% of voting power and at least 80% of value.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：80% voting power 和 80% value 两个都要看。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Consolidated Return Liability and Compliance.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.title: Rule Card - Consolidated Return Liability and Compliance
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---consolidated-return-.content:
Consolidated Return Liability and Compliance
Core Rule
Each member of a consolidated group is jointly and severally liable for the group’s consolidated tax liability, penalties, and interest.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：合并申报不是 parent 自己负责，members 也可能 jointly and severally liable。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-capital-lo.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Corporate Capital Losses.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-capital-lo.title: Rule Card - Corporate Capital Losses
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-capital-lo.content:
Corporate Capital Losses
Core Rule
Corporate capital losses can offset only corporate capital gains. They cannot offset ordinary income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：个人和公司的 capital loss 规则不同，公司 capital loss 不能直接抵 ordinary income。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-distributi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Corporate Distribution Ordering.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-distributi.title: Rule Card - Corporate Distribution Ordering
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-distributi.content:
Corporate Distribution Ordering
Core Rule
A corporate distribution is a dividend to the extent of current and accumulated earnings and profits. Amounts beyond E&P generally reduce stock basis, and amounts beyond basis are capital gain.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：distribution classification 先看 E&P，再看 shareholder basis。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-estimated-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Corporate Estimated Tax Payments.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-estimated-.title: Rule Card - Corporate Estimated Tax Payments
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-estimated-.content:
Corporate Estimated Tax Payments
Core Rule
Corporations generally must make estimated tax payments during the year and may face penalties for underpayment unless they satisfy an available safe method.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：corporate estimated tax 题要看 current-year tax、prior-year tax 和 annualized income method。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-nol-utiliz.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Corporate NOL Utilization.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-nol-utiliz.title: Rule Card - Corporate NOL Utilization
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---corporate-nol-utiliz.content:
Corporate NOL Utilization
Core Rule
Corporate NOL usage depends on the year the NOL arose. Post-2017 NOL carryforwards are generally carried forward indefinitely, but beginning in 2021 they can offset only 80% of taxable income after pre-2018 NOL carryforwards.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：NOL 题第一步永远是看 NOL 年份。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---distributable-net-in.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Distributable Net Income DNI.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---distributable-net-in.title: Rule Card - Distributable Net Income DNI
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---distributable-net-in.content:
Distributable Net Income (DNI)
Core Rule
DNI limits both the amount beneficiaries include in taxable income and the amount the trust can deduct as an income distribution deduction.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：DNI 是 trust deduction 和 beneficiary income 的共同上限。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---equity-compensation-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Equity Compensation Tax Timing.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---equity-compensation-.title: Rule Card - Equity Compensation Tax Timing
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---equity-compensation-.content:
Equity Compensation Tax Timing
Core Rule
The tax treatment of equity compensation depends on the type of award and the relevant date: grant date, vesting date, exercise date, and sale date.
Key Award Types

Nonstatutory stock options
Incentive stock options
Employee stock purchase plans
Restricted stock
Restricted stock units
Stock appreciation rights

Exam Approach

Identify the award type.
Determine whether value is readily determinable.
Locate the taxable event.
Classify the income as ordinary compensation income or capital gain/loss.
Determine basis and holding period.

High-Yield Notes

Nonstatutory options can create ordinary compensation income.
Statutory options may defer regular taxable income, but ISO exercise can create AMT consequences.
Restricted stock generally creates income when restrictions lapse unless a special election applies.
Later sale of stock may create capital gain or loss based on adjusted basis.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：先找 taxable event，再算 amount。不要看到 stock 就直接当 capital gain。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estate-planning-owne.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Estate Planning Ownership and Beneficiary Designations.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estate-planning-owne.title: Rule Card - Estate Planning Ownership and Beneficiary Designations
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estate-planning-owne.content:
Estate Planning Ownership and Beneficiary Designations
Core Rule
Estate planning depends on legal ownership and beneficiary designations. Some assets transfer directly outside probate.
Key Ideas

Wills create a plan for probate assets.
Beneficiary designations can control retirement accounts, life insurance, brokerage accounts, and bank accounts.
Joint tenancy with right of survivorship can transfer assets directly to the surviving owner.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：will 不一定控制所有资产，beneficiary designation 可能优先。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estimated-tax-safe-h.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Estimated Tax Safe Harbors.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estimated-tax-safe-h.title: Rule Card - Estimated Tax Safe Harbors
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---estimated-tax-safe-h.content:
Estimated Tax Safe Harbors
Core Rule
Taxpayers may owe an underpayment penalty if they do not pay enough tax during the year through withholding or timely estimated tax payments.
Safe Harbors
The penalty can generally be avoided if:

the filed return shows less than $1,000 of tax owed; or
the taxpayer paid the lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax.

Higher-Income Rule
Use 110% of prior-year tax instead of 100% when prior-year AGI exceeds $150,000.
Failure-to-Pay Penalty
The failure-to-pay penalty is generally 0.5% of unpaid tax per month, up to 25%.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：看 prior-year AGI 是否超过 $150,000，超过时 prior-year safe harbor 变成 110%。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-tax-credit-l.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Foreign Tax Credit Limitation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-tax-credit-l.title: Rule Card - Foreign Tax Credit Limitation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-tax-credit-l.content:
Foreign Tax Credit Limitation
Core Rule
The foreign tax credit is limited so the credit does not exceed the U.S. tax attributable to foreign-source taxable income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：FTC 是 limited credit，不是 foreign tax paid 全额都能抵。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-earned-incom.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Foreign-Earned Income Exclusion.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-earned-incom.title: Rule Card - Foreign-Earned Income Exclusion
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---foreign-earned-incom.content:
Foreign-Earned Income Exclusion
Core Rule
A qualifying taxpayer may exclude a limited amount of foreign-earned income from U.S. gross income.
Key Requirements

The income must be foreign-earned income.
The taxpayer must have a tax home in a foreign country.
The taxpayer must satisfy either the bona fide residence test or the physical presence test.

Physical Presence Test
The taxpayer must be physically present in one or more foreign countries for at least 330 full days during any 12-consecutive-month period.
2023 Amount

Maximum exclusion: $120,000.

Exam Approach

Confirm the income is earned income.
Confirm the income is earned while working outside the United States.
Test qualification.
Apply the exclusion limit.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：先判断 qualification，再用 exclusion amount。不要先套 $120,000。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---gift-tax-annual-excl.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Gift Tax Annual Exclusion.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---gift-tax-annual-excl.title: Rule Card - Gift Tax Annual Exclusion
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---gift-tax-annual-excl.content:
Gift Tax Annual Exclusion
Core Rule
The donor may exclude the first $17,000 of gifts made to each donee in 2023.
Gift Splitting
A gift by either spouse may be treated as made one-half by each spouse. This can create a $34,000 exclusion per donee.
Limitation
The annual exclusion is generally not available for a gift of a future interest.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：annual exclusion 是 per donee，不是 donor 一年总共只有 $17,000。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---guaranteed-payments-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Guaranteed Payments to Partners.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---guaranteed-payments-.title: Rule Card - Guaranteed Payments to Partners
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---guaranteed-payments-.content:
Guaranteed Payments to Partners
Core Rule
Guaranteed payments are payments to partners for services or use of capital made without regard to the partnership’s income. They are deductible by the partnership and taxable to the partner.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：guaranteed payment 不是 profit distribution，它像 partner 的固定补偿。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---home-sale-exclusion.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Home Sale Exclusion.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---home-sale-exclusion.title: Rule Card - Home Sale Exclusion
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---home-sale-exclusion.content:
Home Sale Exclusion
Core Rule
Gain from the sale of a principal residence may be excluded up to 250,000 for single, married filing separately, and head of household taxpayers, or 500,000 for married filing jointly and certain surviving spouses.
Qualification
The taxpayer generally must have owned and used the property as a principal residence for at least two years during the five-year period ending on the sale date.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：ownership test 和 use test 都要看，但不一定是连续的同一两年。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---hot-assets.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Hot Assets.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---hot-assets.title: Rule Card - Hot Assets
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---hot-assets.content:
Hot Assets
Core Rule
Hot assets are partnership assets that generate ordinary income rather than capital gain, such as inventory and unrealized receivables.
Exam Impact
Hot assets can cause part of the gain on sale of a partnership interest to be ordinary income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：partnership interest sale 通常 capital，但 hot assets 会切出 ordinary income。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---ira-contribution-and.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - IRA Contribution and Distribution Tax Treatment.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---ira-contribution-and.title: Rule Card - IRA Contribution and Distribution Tax Treatment
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---ira-contribution-and.content:
IRA Contribution and Distribution Tax Treatment
2023 Contribution Limits

Under age 50: $6,500.
Age 50 or older: $7,500.
The limit applies to the combined total of traditional and Roth IRA contributions.

Distribution Treatment

Nondeductible traditional IRA distribution: principal nontaxable, earnings taxable.
Deductible traditional IRA distribution: principal taxable, earnings taxable.
Qualified Roth IRA distribution: principal nontaxable, earnings nontaxable.
Nonqualified Roth IRA distribution: principal nontaxable, earnings taxable.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：IRA distribution 题要分 principal 和 earnings。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---installment-sale-gro.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Installment Sale Gross Profit Percentage.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---installment-sale-gro.title: Rule Card - Installment Sale Gross Profit Percentage
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---installment-sale-gro.content:
Installment Sale Gross Profit Percentage
Core Formula
Gross profit = Sales price - Adjusted basis
Gross profit percentage = Gross profit / Sales price
Gain recognized = Cash collections excluding interest x Gross profit percentage
Chinese Note

易错提醒：interest is ordinary income and is not included in cash collections for installment sale gain.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---involuntary-conversi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Involuntary Conversions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---involuntary-conversi.title: Rule Card - Involuntary Conversions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---involuntary-conversi.content:
Involuntary Conversions
Core Rule
Gain from an involuntary conversion can be deferred when the taxpayer reinvests in similar replacement property within the required period.
Basis Idea
Basis in replacement property generally equals cost of replacement property minus deferred gain.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：involuntary conversion rules defer gains; losses are generally recognized.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---kiddie-tax.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Kiddie Tax.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---kiddie-tax.title: Rule Card - Kiddie Tax
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---kiddie-tax.content:
Kiddie Tax
Core Rule
The net unearned income of certain dependent children is taxed at the parents’ tax rate.
Who Is Commonly Covered

A dependent child under age 18.
A child age 18 through under 24 who is a full-time student and does not provide more than half of their own support.

Exam Approach

Determine whether the child is subject to kiddie tax.
Separate earned income from unearned income.
Compute net unearned income.
Tax the appropriate amount at the parents’ rate.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：kiddie tax 主要针对 unearned income，不是孩子所有收入都按父母税率。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---like-kind-exchange-t.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Like-Kind Exchange Timing and Boot.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---like-kind-exchange-t.title: Rule Card - Like-Kind Exchange Timing and Boot
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---like-kind-exchange-t.content:
Like-Kind Exchange Timing and Boot
Core Rule
Like-kind exchange treatment can defer gain for qualifying business or investment real property.
Timing Requirements

Replacement property must be identified within 45 days.
Replacement property must be received by the earlier of 180 days after transfer or the tax return due date, including extensions.

Boot
Boot, such as cash, debt relief, or nonqualifying property, can trigger recognized gain.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：like-kind exchange 现在重点是 real property，且 45/180 天必须记牢。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---limits-on-tax-planni.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Limits on Tax Planning.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---limits-on-tax-planni.title: Rule Card - Limits on Tax Planning
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---limits-on-tax-planni.content:
Limits on Tax Planning
Core Rule
Tax planning strategies are limited by statutes, regulations, disclosure requirements, judicial doctrines, economic substance, business purpose, and anti-abuse rules.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：tax planning 合法不等于任意安排，题目常用 substance/business purpose 卡答案。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---loss-limitation-orde.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Loss Limitation Ordering.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---loss-limitation-orde.title: Rule Card - Loss Limitation Ordering
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---loss-limitation-orde.content:
Loss Limitation Ordering
Core Rule
Individual business losses must pass through four limitations before they are deductible.
Ordering

Tax basis limitation
At-risk limitation
Passive activity loss limitation
Excess business loss limitation

Exam Approach

Start with the total allocated loss.
Limit the loss to tax basis.
Limit the remaining loss to at-risk amount.
Determine whether the loss is passive.
Apply the excess business loss limitation after PAL rules.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：这类题先写顺序。顺序错了，后面数字通常都会错。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---mom-and-pop-rental-r.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Mom-and-Pop Rental Real Estate Exception.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---mom-and-pop-rental-r.title: Rule Card - Mom-and-Pop Rental Real Estate Exception
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---mom-and-pop-rental-r.content:
Mom-and-Pop Rental Real Estate Exception
Core Rule
An individual taxpayer may deduct up to $25,000 of net passive losses from rental real estate if the taxpayer actively participates and owns at least 10% of the rental real estate activity.
Phase-Out

The 25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of AGI over 100,000.
The allowance is fully eliminated when AGI exceeds $150,000.

Exam Approach

Confirm the activity is rental real estate.
Confirm active participation.
Confirm at least 10% ownership.
Apply the AGI phase-out.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：mom-and-pop 是 active participation，不是 material participation。要求较低，但有 AGI phase-out。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---participation-exempt.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Participation Exemption DRD.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---participation-exempt.title: Rule Card - Participation Exemption DRD
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---participation-exempt.content:
Participation Exemption DRD
Core Rule
The participation exemption may allow a 100% dividends-received deduction for certain foreign-source dividends paid to a U.S. C corporation by a specified foreign corporation.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：100% DRD 不代表所有 foreign income 都免税，Subpart F、GILTI 等可能不适用。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-inside-b.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Partnership Inside Basis.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-inside-b.title: Rule Card - Partnership Inside Basis
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-inside-b.content:
Partnership Inside Basis
Core Rule
Inside basis is the partnership’s basis in its assets. When property is contributed, the partnership generally takes a carryover basis in the contributed property.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：inside basis 用来看 partnership 持有资产的 basis，不是 partner 的 outside basis。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-liquidat.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Partnership Liquidating Distributions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-liquidat.title: Rule Card - Partnership Liquidating Distributions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-liquidat.content:
Partnership Liquidating Distributions
Core Rule
A liquidating distribution terminates the partner’s interest in the partnership. The partner’s remaining outside basis is allocated to assets received.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：liquidating distribution 的目标是把 outside basis 用完并结束 partner interest。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-nonliqui.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Partnership Nonliquidating Distributions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-nonliqui.title: Rule Card - Partnership Nonliquidating Distributions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-nonliqui.content:
Partnership Nonliquidating Distributions
Core Rule
Nonliquidating distributions generally reduce the partner’s outside basis. Cash distributions in excess of outside basis can trigger gain.
Basis Allocation
Basis is generally assigned first to cash, then hot assets, then other property.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：cash distribution 可能触发 gain；property distribution 通常先看 basis allocation。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-outside-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Partnership Outside Basis.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-outside-.title: Rule Card - Partnership Outside Basis
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---partnership-outside-.content:
Partnership Outside Basis
Core Rule
Outside basis is the partner’s basis in the partnership interest. It is used to determine loss deductibility, gain on distributions, and gain or loss on sale of the partnership interest.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：outside basis 属于 partner；inside basis 属于 partnership assets。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---passive-activity-los.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Passive Activity Loss Limitation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---passive-activity-los.title: Rule Card - Passive Activity Loss Limitation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---passive-activity-los.content:
Passive Activity Loss Limitation
Core Rule
A passive activity loss can generally offset only passive activity income. It cannot offset active income or portfolio income.
Income Categories

Active income: wages, business income from material participation.
Passive income: income from activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate.
Portfolio income: dividends, interest, capital gains, and similar investment income.

Material Participation
A common material participation test is participation for more than 500 hours during the tax year.
Suspended Losses
PALs that cannot be used are suspended and carried forward. When the taxpayer disposes of the passive activity, remaining suspended PALs may become deductible.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：dividends 和 capital gains 通常是 portfolio income，不是 passive income。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---political-and-lobbyi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Political and Lobbying Restrictions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---political-and-lobbyi.title: Rule Card - Political and Lobbying Restrictions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---political-and-lobbyi.content:
Political and Lobbying Restrictions
Core Rule
Section 501(c)(3) organizations cannot participate in political campaign activity, and substantial lobbying can jeopardize exempt status.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：nonpartisan voter education may be different from prohibited campaign intervention。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---present-interest-vs-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Present Interest vs Future Interest Gifts.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---present-interest-vs-.title: Rule Card - Present Interest vs Future Interest Gifts
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---present-interest-vs-.content:
Present Interest vs Future Interest Gifts
Present Interest
A present interest gives the donee a current right to use, possess, or enjoy the property. It generally qualifies for the annual exclusion.
Future Interest
A future interest delays the donee’s right to use, possess, or enjoy the property. It generally does not qualify for the annual exclusion.
Exam Approach

Identify what the donee can do now.
Determine whether enjoyment is postponed.
Apply or deny the annual exclusion.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：看 donee 现在能不能享有利益，不是看 title 是否已经转移。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---profits-interest-vs-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Profits Interest vs Capital Interest.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---profits-interest-vs-.title: Rule Card - Profits Interest vs Capital Interest
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---profits-interest-vs-.content:
Profits Interest vs Capital Interest
Profits Interest
A profits interest gives the partner a right to share in future profits or losses. A profits interest received for services is generally not taxable when received.
Capital Interest
A capital interest gives the partner a right to share in partnership net assets upon liquidation. A capital interest received for services is generally taxable compensation.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：profits interest 看未来利润；capital interest 看现在清算能拿到的资产份额。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---qbi-deduction-overvi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - QBI Deduction Overview.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---qbi-deduction-overvi.title: Rule Card - QBI Deduction Overview
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---qbi-deduction-overvi.content:
QBI Deduction Overview
Core Rule
The QBI deduction is generally available to individual owners of flow-through entities and is generally 20% of qualified business income, subject to limitations.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：QBI 是 owner-level deduction，不是 entity-level deduction。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---real-estate-professi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Real Estate Professional Exception.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---real-estate-professi.title: Rule Card - Real Estate Professional Exception
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---real-estate-professi.content:
Real Estate Professional Exception
Core Rule
If the taxpayer qualifies as a real estate professional, rental real estate activities are treated as active rather than passive, and the PAL limitation does not apply.
Tests
The taxpayer must satisfy both tests:

More than 50% of the taxpayer’s personal services during the year are performed in real estate businesses.
The taxpayer performs more than 750 hours of services in real estate businesses during the year.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：real estate professional 必须两个条件都满足，不能只看 750 hours。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recipient-basis-in-g.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Recipient Basis in Gifted Property.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recipient-basis-in-g.title: Rule Card - Recipient Basis in Gifted Property
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recipient-basis-in-g.content:
Recipient Basis in Gifted Property
Core Rule
The recipient of a gift generally does not recognize taxable income when receiving the gift.
Basis Rule
The general basis rule for gifted property is carryover basis: the recipient’s basis equals the donor’s basis, adjusted for gift tax paid attributable to appreciation when applicable.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：recipient 收到 gift 通常不确认 income，但以后出售时 basis 很重要。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recourse-vs-nonrecou.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Recourse vs Nonrecourse Debt Allocation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recourse-vs-nonrecou.title: Rule Card - Recourse vs Nonrecourse Debt Allocation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---recourse-vs-nonrecou.content:
Recourse vs Nonrecourse Debt Allocation
Recourse Debt
Recourse debt is generally allocated to partners who bear the economic risk of loss.
Nonrecourse Debt
Nonrecourse debt is generally allocated according to partnership sharing rules because no partner bears personal liability.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：debt allocation 会影响 outside basis，但 at-risk treatment 可能不同。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-basis-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Related Party Basis and Holding Period.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-basis-.title: Rule Card - Related Party Basis and Holding Period
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-basis-.content:
Related Party Basis and Holding Period
Core Rule
Related party transactions can alter basis, gain/loss recognition, holding period, and timing of deductions and income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：related party 题经常不是问有没有 gain，而是问 character、basis、timing。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-constr.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Related Party Constructive Ownership.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-constr.title: Rule Card - Related Party Constructive Ownership
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-constr.content:
Related Party Constructive Ownership
Core Rule
Constructive ownership rules can treat stock owned by certain family members, entities, or related parties as owned by the taxpayer.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：related party 不只看直接 ownership，还要看 attribution。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-loss-d.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Related Party Loss Disallowance.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-loss-d.title: Rule Card - Related Party Loss Disallowance
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---related-party-loss-d.content:
Related Party Loss Disallowance
Core Rule
Losses from sales or exchanges between related parties are generally disallowed.
Later Sale
If the related buyer later sells the property at a gain, the previously disallowed loss may reduce the buyer’s gain, subject to limits.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：related-party loss is disallowed now, but may affect later gain calculation.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---retirement-distribut.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Retirement Distribution Penalties and Exceptions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---retirement-distribut.title: Rule Card - Retirement Distribution Penalties and Exceptions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---retirement-distribut.content:
Retirement Distribution Penalties and Exceptions
Core Rule
Premature taxable retirement distributions may be subject to a 10% additional penalty tax before age 59 1/2, unless an exception applies.
Common Exceptions

Disability
Death
Certain medical expenses
Qualified education expenses for IRAs
First-time homebuyer IRA distribution, subject to a $10,000 limit
Certain birth or adoption distributions
Qualified domestic relations order for certain plans

Chinese Note

易错提醒：penalty 是加在 taxable distribution 上。先判断 taxable，再判断 penalty。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-aaa-an.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - S Corporation AAA and Distribution Ordering.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-aaa-an.title: Rule Card - S Corporation AAA and Distribution Ordering
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-aaa-an.content:
S Corporation AAA and Distribution Ordering
Core Rule
The accumulated adjustments account (AAA) tracks accumulated S corporation earnings. Distribution ordering depends on whether the S corporation has accumulated C corporation E&P.
Key Idea
AAA helps determine whether distributions are tax-free recovery of basis, dividends from C corporation E&P, or capital gain.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：有 C corp E&P 时，S corp distribution ordering 会更复杂。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-built-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - S Corporation Built-In Gains Tax.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-built-.title: Rule Card - S Corporation Built-In Gains Tax
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-built-.content:
S Corporation Built-In Gains Tax
Core Rule
An S corporation may owe corporate-level built-in gains tax when a former C corporation sells or distributes appreciated assets after electing S status.
Trigger
Built-in gain exists when, on the S election date, the FMV of corporate assets exceeds their adjusted basis.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：S corp 通常 pass-through，但 former C corp 的 built-in gain 可能还会被 corporate-level tax 抓住。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-stock-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - S Corporation Stock and Debt Basis.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-stock-.title: Rule Card - S Corporation Stock and Debt Basis
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-stock-.content:
S Corporation Stock and Debt Basis
Core Rule
S corporation shareholders track both stock basis and debt basis. Loss deductions are limited by basis and other limitation rules.
Stock Basis Increases

Initial contributions
Additional contributions
Ordinary business income
Separately stated income and gain
Tax-exempt income

Stock Basis Decreases

Distributions
Nondeductible expenses
Separately stated losses and deductions
Ordinary business loss

Chinese Note

易错提醒：S corp loss 先看 stock basis，再看 debt basis 和其他 limitations。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-termin.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - S Corporation Termination.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-termin.title: Rule Card - S Corporation Termination
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---s-corporation-termin.content:
S Corporation Termination
Core Rule
S corporation status can terminate by voluntary revocation, failure to meet S corporation eligibility requirements, or excessive passive investment income when the corporation has accumulated C corporation E&P.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：excess passive investment income 可能影响 S status，尤其是有 C corp E&P 的 S corp。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---sale-of-partnership-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Sale of Partnership Interest.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---sale-of-partnership-.title: Rule Card - Sale of Partnership Interest
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---sale-of-partnership-.content:
Sale of Partnership Interest
Core Rule
Sale of a partnership interest generally produces capital gain or loss. However, gain attributable to hot assets is ordinary income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：amount realized may include debt relief, not just cash received.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1231-five-ye.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 1231 Five-Year Lookback.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1231-five-ye.title: Rule Card - Section 1231 Five-Year Lookback
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1231-five-ye.content:
Section 1231 Five-Year Lookback
Core Rule
Net Section 1231 gains are generally long-term capital gains, but the five-year lookback rule can recharacterize current Section 1231 gain as ordinary income to the extent of prior net Section 1231 losses deducted as ordinary losses.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：1231 gain 不是自动 capital gain，要先 look back 五年。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1244-and-qsb.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 1244 and QSBS.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1244-and-qsb.title: Rule Card - Section 1244 and QSBS
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1244-and-qsb.content:
Section 1244 and QSBS
Section 1244
Original small business stockholders may receive ordinary loss treatment up to 50,000, or 100,000 for married filing jointly.
QSBS
A noncorporate shareholder who holds qualified small business stock for more than five years may generally exclude 100% of gain, subject to limits.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：Section 1244 helps losses; QSBS helps gains.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1245-and-125.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 1245 and 1250 Recapture.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1245-and-125.title: Rule Card - Section 1245 and 1250 Recapture
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-1245-and-125.content:
Section 1245 and 1250 Recapture
Section 1245
Applies mainly to depreciable personal property. Gain is recaptured as ordinary income to the extent of depreciation taken.
Section 1250
Applies to depreciable real property. Recapture generally focuses on depreciation in excess of straight-line depreciation.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：1245 常见于 personal property；1250 常见于 real property。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-291-recaptur.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 291 Recapture for C Corporations.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-291-recaptur.title: Rule Card - Section 291 Recapture for C Corporations
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-291-recaptur.content:
Section 291 Recapture for C Corporations
Core Rule
Section 291 can require C corporations to recognize additional ordinary income on certain real property dispositions beyond the normal Section 1250 recapture.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：Section 291 is a C corporation-specific recapture rule.

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-351-corporat.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 351 Corporate Formation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-351-corporat.title: Rule Card - Section 351 Corporate Formation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-351-corporat.content:
Section 351 Corporate Formation
Core Rule
Formation of a corporation is generally nontaxable if property is transferred to the corporation solely in exchange for stock and the transferors control the corporation immediately after the exchange.
Control Requirement
The transferors must own at least 80% of voting stock and at least 80% of nonvoting stock immediately after the exchange.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：services 不算 Section 351 property contribution。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-382-ownershi.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 382 Ownership Change Limitation.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-382-ownershi.title: Rule Card - Section 382 Ownership Change Limitation
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-382-ownershi.content:
Section 382 Ownership Change Limitation
Core Rule
Section 382 limits the use of pre-change NOLs after a loss corporation has an ownership change. The rule prevents profitable corporations from buying loss corporations mainly to use their NOL carryforwards.
Exam Approach

Identify whether the corporation is a loss corporation.
Determine whether an ownership change occurred.
Apply the Section 382 annual limitation to pre-change losses.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：Section 382 不是取消 NOL，而是限制每年能用多少。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-501(c)(3)-qu.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 501(c)(3) Qualification.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-501(c)(3)-qu.title: Rule Card - Section 501(c)(3) Qualification
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-501(c)(3)-qu.content:
Section 501(c)(3) Qualification
Core Rule
A Section 501(c)(3) organization must be organized as a corporation, unincorporated association, or trust; have an exempt purpose; avoid private benefit; and comply with political and lobbying restrictions.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：tax-exempt status 是资格问题，不是自动获得。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-529-qualifie.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 529 Qualified Tuition Programs.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-529-qualifie.title: Rule Card - Section 529 Qualified Tuition Programs
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-529-qualifie.content:
Section 529 Qualified Tuition Programs
Core Rule
Section 529 plans are tax-favored education funding arrangements. Distributions are tax-free to the extent used for qualified education expenses.
Types

Prepaid tuition plans
Educational savings plans

Taxable Portion
If distributions exceed qualified expenses, the earnings portion of the excess distribution may be taxable and may also be subject to an additional 10% penalty.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：529 不是取出来都免税，必须对上 qualified education expenses。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-754-election.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Section 754 Election.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-754-election.title: Rule Card - Section 754 Election
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---section-754-election.content:
Section 754 Election
Core Rule
A Section 754 election allows optional basis adjustments to partnership assets after transfers of partnership interests or certain distributions.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：754 election 是 partnership-level election，用来调整 inside basis。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---stock-redemptions.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Stock Redemptions.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---stock-redemptions.title: Rule Card - Stock Redemptions
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---stock-redemptions.content:
Stock Redemptions
Core Rule
When a corporation buys back shareholder stock, the redemption may be treated as a sale or exchange, or as a dividend to the extent of E&P.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：redemption 不一定是 sale treatment，要判断是否符合 sale/exchange 条件。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---subpart-f-and-gilti-.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Subpart F and GILTI Overview.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---subpart-f-and-gilti-.title: Rule Card - Subpart F and GILTI Overview
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---subpart-f-and-gilti-.content:
Subpart F and GILTI Overview
Core Rule
Subpart F and GILTI are anti-deferral regimes that can require U.S. shareholders of controlled foreign corporations to include certain foreign income currently.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：没有实际 dividend，也可能有 current U.S. taxable inclusion。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---substantial-presence.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Substantial Presence Test.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---substantial-presence.title: Rule Card - Substantial Presence Test
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---substantial-presence.content:
Substantial Presence Test
Core Rule
The substantial presence test can cause a foreign individual to be treated as a U.S. resident for tax purposes based on days of presence in the United States.
Exam Approach

Count current-year U.S. days.
Apply the weighted multi-year day formula when required.
Check exceptions or treaty relief.

Chinese Note

易错提醒：residency test 和 source rules 是两个不同问题。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---transfer-pricing-arm.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Transfer Pricing Arm's-Length Standard.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---transfer-pricing-arm.title: Rule Card - Transfer Pricing Arm's-Length Standard
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---transfer-pricing-arm.content:
Transfer Pricing Arm’s-Length Standard
Core Rule
Controlled transactions must be priced as if unrelated parties were dealing at arm’s length. The IRS may adjust income, deductions, credits, or allowances to reflect true taxable income.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：transfer pricing 的核心是 controlled transaction 是否像 unrelated parties 一样定价。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---trust-income-distrib.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Trust Income Distribution Deduction.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---trust-income-distrib.title: Rule Card - Trust Income Distribution Deduction
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---trust-income-distrib.content:
Trust Income Distribution Deduction
Core Rule
A trust may deduct income distributed or required to be distributed to beneficiaries, limited by DNI and other trust rules.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：trust distribution deduction 防止同一收入在 trust 和 beneficiary 双重纳税。

04-卡片笔记/rule-card---unrelated-business-i.filePath: 04 卡片笔记/Rule Card - Unrelated Business Income UBI.md
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---unrelated-business-i.title: Rule Card - Unrelated Business Income UBI
04-卡片笔记/rule-card---unrelated-business-i.content:
Unrelated Business Income (UBI)
Core Rule
UBI is income from a trade or business that is regularly carried on and not substantially related to the organization’s exempt purpose. It may be taxable even though the organization is tax-exempt.
Chinese Note

易错提醒：判断 UBI 三步：trade/business、regularly carried on、not related to exempt purpose。

TCP 1 Module 1 Updates
2026 Standard Deduction

Single: $16,100
Head of household: $24,150

Married filing separately: $16,100

Additional Standard Deduction for Age 65 or Older and/or Blindness

Unmarried, one qualified status: $2,050
Unmarried, both 65 and blind: $4,100
Married, one qualified taxpayer: $1,650
Married, both 65 and blind for one qualified taxpayer: $3,300
Married, two qualified taxpayers each 65 or blind: $3,300
Married, two qualified taxpayers both 65 and blind: $6,600

Charitable Deduction if Standard Deduction Taken
Individual taxpayers who do not itemize can deduct cash contributions to public charities up to:

$1,000
$2,000 for MFJ

Itemized Deduction Updates

Medical expenses: deductible in excess of 7.5% of AGI.
State and local taxes: limited to $40,400 in 2026.
Charitable contributions: subject to a 0.5% of AGI floor.
Casualty/theft losses: limited to federal or state-declared disasters, with per-casualty and AGI limitations.

TCP 1 Module 4 Updates
RMDs From Traditional 401(k)s
RMDs from traditional 401(k)s must begin by April 1 of the year after the later of:

the year the employee reaches age 73, if born between 1951 and 1959;
the year the employee reaches age 75, if born in 1960 or later; or
the year the employee terminates employment with the plan sponsor.

Roth 401(k) plans are not subject to these RMD requirements.
Failure-to-take-RMD penalty:

25%
reduced to 10% if corrected in a timely manner

2026 IRA Limits

Under age 50: $7,500
Age 50 or older: $8,600
Married under age 50: $15,000 total
Married age 50 or older: $17,200 total

2026 Traditional IRA Deduction Phase-Out
If taxpayer participates in an employer-sponsored retirement plan:

Unmarried: 81,000-91,000
MFJ: 129,000-149,000

Special spousal rule if taxpayer is not an active participant but spouse is:

MFJ: 242,000-252,000
MFS: 0-10,000

2026 Roth IRA Contribution Phase-Out

Unmarried: 153,000-168,000
MFJ: 242,000-252,000
MFS: 0-10,000

Trump Accounts
Trump accounts are tax-deferred investment accounts for children under age 18 with a valid Social Security number.

Starting July 4, 2026, eligible children under 18 may open and contribute.
U.S. citizen children born between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2028, with a Social Security number, receive a one-time $1,000 federal contribution under the pilot program.
Employers may contribute up to $2,500 per year for an employee or dependent.
Maximum total contribution: $5,000 per year.
No deduction is allowed for contributions.
Employer and federal pilot contributions are excluded from income.
No distributions before the calendar year the beneficiary turns 18.
At age 18 or older, regular traditional IRA distribution rules apply.

TCP 2 Updates
Section 1244 Small Business Stock
Maximum ordinary loss deduction:

MFJ: $100,000
Other individual filers: $50,000

Section 1202 QSBS
Aggregate gross assets limitation:

Stock issued on or before July 4, 2025: $50 million
Stock issued after July 4, 2025: $75 million

Maximum exclusion per shareholder:

Stock acquired on or before July 4, 2025: greater of 10 times basis or 10 million (5 million if MFS)
Stock acquired after July 4, 2025: greater of 10 times basis or 15 million (7.5 million if MFS) for 2026

If the exclusion percentage is less than 100%, the 28% capital gain rate applies to the nonexcluded portion of the QSBS gain within the maximum exclusion amount.
Consolidated Taxable Income Calculation
Updated consolidated taxable income steps:

Calculate each member’s stand-alone taxable income.
Remove effects of intercompany transactions.
Remove items determined at the consolidated level.
Combine member taxable incomes.
Apply consolidated-level items.

Consolidated-level items include capital gains/losses, Section 1231 gains/losses, NOL, charitable contribution deduction, and DRD.

TCP 1 Module 1 - Compliance and Tax Planning Considerations
Module Purpose
This module explains how individual taxpayers recognize income, plan deductions, manage timing decisions, and avoid penalties. It also introduces several high-frequency TCP topics: equity compensation, below-market loans, foreign-earned income exclusion, AMT, kiddie tax, FSA/HSA rules, standard vs. itemized deductions, estimated tax payments, and year-end planning.
H - Highlight
Rules and Thresholds

Equity compensation tax timing depends on the award type and key dates.
Below-market loans may create imputed interest.
Foreign-earned income may be excluded if the taxpayer satisfies a qualification test.
Timing decisions should compare after-tax results using present value.
AMTI starts with regular taxable income and then applies AMT adjustments and preference items.
Kiddie tax applies to net unearned income of certain dependent children.
FSAs generally have a use-it-or-lose-it feature; HSAs can accumulate.
Taxpayers compare standard deduction with itemized deductions.
Estimated tax penalties can be avoided through safe harbors.

Key Numbers From This Module

Foreign-earned income exclusion: up to $120,000 for 2023.
Physical presence test: 330 full days in a foreign country during any 12-consecutive-month period.
ISO holding period: at least 2 years after grant date and at least 1 year after exercise date.
ISO annual exercise limit: $100,000.
De minimis loan exception: $10,000 or less, subject to limitations.
Gift loans of $100,000 or less: special limitation based on net investment income.
HSA 2023 contribution limit: 3,850 individual; 7,750 family; additional $1,000 for age 55 or older.
2023 standard deduction: 13,850 single; 20,800 head of household; $27,700 married filing jointly.
Estimated tax safe harbor: less than 1,000 owed, or pay the lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax; 110% if prior-year AGI exceeds 150,000.
Failure-to-pay penalty: generally 0.5% per month, up to 25%.

A - Ask

What type of compensation or transaction is being tested?
What is the taxable event?
Is the income ordinary income, capital gain, or excluded?
Does a threshold, phase-out, holding period, or exception apply?
Is the question asking for tax liability, taxable income, basis, or planning advice?
Would accelerating or deferring income/deductions improve the after-tax result?

R - Rephrase

For equity compensation, identify the award type before calculating income.
For below-market loans, the tax law may treat foregone interest as if it had been paid.
For foreign-earned income, qualification comes before the exclusion amount.
For timing decisions, compare the present value of tax paid or saved.
For AMT, start with regular taxable income and adjust to AMTI.
For deduction planning, standard deduction is the baseline; itemizing only helps when qualified itemized deductions exceed it.
For estimated tax, safe harbor rules matter as much as the final tax due.

N - Network

S - Synthesize
High-Frequency Rules

Equity compensation questions are usually tax timing questions.
Below-market loans convert a missing interest payment into deemed tax consequences.
Foreign-earned income exclusion requires either the bona fide residence test or physical presence test.
AMT adjusts regular taxable income for items treated differently under AMT rules.
Kiddie tax shifts part of a child’s unearned income to the parents’ tax rate.
HSA is more flexible than FSA because unused HSA funds can accumulate.
Bunching itemized deductions can create a benefit when annual itemized deductions are close to the standard deduction.

Common Traps

Treating all stock-related compensation as capital gain.
Forgetting that ISO exercise can create an AMT preference item.
Applying the foreign-earned income exclusion before checking qualification.
Comparing future tax amounts without discounting to present value.
Assuming itemized deductions always help.
Using the 100% prior-year estimated tax safe harbor when the 110% rule applies.

TCP 1 Module 2 - Loss Limitations
Module Purpose
This module explains the four main limitations on an individual taxpayer’s ability to deduct business losses: tax basis, at-risk amount, passive activity loss rules, and excess business loss limitation.
H - Highlight
Four Loss Limitation Hurdles

Tax basis limitation
At-risk limitation
Passive activity loss (PAL) limitation
Excess business loss limitation

Key Numbers

Material participation common test: more than 500 hours during the tax year.
Mom-and-pop rental real estate allowance: up to $25,000.
Mom-and-pop phase-out starts when AGI exceeds $100,000.
Mom-and-pop allowance is fully eliminated when AGI exceeds $150,000.
Real estate professional test: more than 50% of personal services in real estate businesses and more than 750 hours of services.
2023 excess business loss threshold: 578,000 for married filing jointly; 289,000 for all other taxpayers.

A - Ask

Is the taxpayer’s loss limited by tax basis?
Is the taxpayer economically at risk for the loss?
Is the activity active, passive, or portfolio?
Does the taxpayer materially participate?
Is the activity rental real estate?
Does the mom-and-pop exception apply?
Does the excess business loss limitation apply after PAL rules?

R - Rephrase

A loss must clear tax basis before it can be deducted.
A loss must also clear the at-risk limitation.
Passive losses generally offset only passive income.
Certain rental real estate losses can be deducted under the mom-and-pop exception.
Real estate professionals can treat rental real estate activities as active if the tests are met.
Excess business losses are limited after the passive activity loss rules.

N - Network

High-Frequency Rules

Tax basis and at-risk limits often apply before passive loss limits.
PALs generally cannot offset active or portfolio income.
Suspended PALs can become deductible when the taxpayer disposes of the passive activity.
The excess business loss limitation applies to both active and passive business activities after PAL rules.

Common Traps

Skipping directly to PAL without checking tax basis and at-risk amount.
Treating portfolio income as passive income.
Forgetting the mom-and-pop phase-out.
Forgetting that real estate professional status requires both the 50% test and the 750-hour test.
Applying the excess business loss limitation before PAL rules.

TCP 1 Module 3 - Gift Tax and Charitable Donations
Module Purpose
This module explains gift taxation, the unified transfer tax system, taxable gifts, annual and unlimited exclusions, present vs. future interests, complete vs. incomplete gifts, recipient basis, and charitable contribution planning for noncash property.
H - Highlight
Key Numbers

Unified credit base for 2023: cumulative taxable transfers of $12,920,000.
Annual gift tax exclusion for 2023: $17,000 per donee.
Gift splitting can create a $34,000 annual exclusion per donee.
Cash charitable contributions to public charities: generally subject to a 60% of AGI limitation.
Ordinary income property contributions: generally subject to a 50% of AGI limitation.
LTCG property contributions: generally subject to a 30% of AGI limitation.
Excess charitable contributions may be carried forward for five years.
Noncash contributions over $500 require Form 8283.
Noncash contributions over $5,000 generally require a qualified appraisal.

A - Ask

Is the transfer a taxable gift?
Is the gift a present interest or future interest?
Is the gift complete or incomplete?
Does an annual exclusion or unlimited exclusion apply?
What is the recipient’s basis?
Is charitable property ordinary income property or long-term capital gain property?
Is tangible personal property used for a related or unrelated charitable purpose?
Which AGI limitation applies?
Is substantiation required?

R - Rephrase

A gift tax issue starts with whether the transfer is for less than adequate consideration.
The annual exclusion generally requires a present interest.
Only complete gifts are subject to gift tax and eligible for the annual exclusion.
The recipient generally does not recognize income from receiving a gift.
Charitable deductions for noncash property depend on property type, holding period, appreciation, and charitable use.

S - Synthesize

The annual exclusion applies per donee, per year.
Future interest gifts generally do not qualify for the annual exclusion.
Transfers between spouses may qualify for the unlimited marital deduction.
Ordinary income property deductions are limited to the lesser of adjusted basis or FMV.
LTCG property deductions are generally based on FMV, unless a special limitation applies.
Tangible personal property used for an unrelated purpose can reduce the deduction to adjusted basis.

Applying the annual exclusion to a future interest gift.
Forgetting gift splitting.
Treating every noncash charitable donation as deductible at FMV.

TCP 1 Module 4 - Personal Financial Planning
Module Purpose
This module covers tax-aware personal financial planning: retirement plans, IRAs, annuities, investment risk, education funding, insurance, after-tax return on investment, and estate planning.
H - Highlight
Retirement Planning

401(k) employee elective deferral for 2023: 22,500; 30,000 if age 50 or older.
Combined employee and employer 401(k) limit for 2023: 66,000; 73,500 if age 50 or older.
IRA contribution limit for 2023: 6,500; 7,500 if age 50 or older.
Traditional retirement contributions generally create tax benefit now.
Roth contributions generally create tax benefit later.
Premature taxable distributions may trigger a 10% additional tax before age 59 1/2, subject to exceptions.
Roth qualified distributions generally require age 59 1/2 and a five-year holding period.

Education Planning

Section 529 qualified tuition programs may be prepaid tuition plans or educational savings plans.
Qualified education distributions can be tax-free.
Excess distributions may create taxable earnings and a 10% additional penalty.
Student loan interest deduction is limited to $2,500.
Scholarships and fellowships can be tax-exempt when requirements are satisfied.

Insurance and Risk

Risk management methods include avoidance, reduction, retention, and transfer.
Long-term care benefit triggers include inability to perform at least two activities of daily living for at least 90 days, or substantial cognitive impairment.

Investment Return

ROI compares gain or loss to investment cost.
After-tax rate of return adjusts the investment return for tax.

Estate Planning

Wills do not override beneficiary designations.
Beneficiary designations can transfer assets directly.
Joint tenancy with right of survivorship can transfer ownership outside probate.

A - Ask

Is the account traditional or Roth?
Is the contribution deductible, nondeductible, or after-tax?
Is the distribution taxable, nontaxable, or partially taxable?
Does a penalty apply?
Does an exception apply?
Is the education distribution qualified?
Is investment risk systematic or nonsystematic?
Does estate transfer happen through probate, beneficiary designation, or joint ownership?

R - Rephrase

Traditional accounts usually shift tax to later; Roth accounts usually pay tax now for potential tax-free treatment later.
Retirement distribution questions require account type, contribution type, age, holding period, and exception analysis.
Education accounts are tax-favored only to the extent distributions are used for qualified expenses.
Insurance planning is about matching risk severity and frequency with the right risk management method.
Estate planning depends heavily on legal ownership and beneficiary designations.

N - Network

S - Synthesize
High-Frequency Rules

Identify the account type before deciding taxability.
Roth treatment depends heavily on qualified distribution rules.
Self-employed retirement plans use different contribution formulas and caps.
Education account taxation depends on qualified expenses and earnings portion.
Long-term care insurance uses ADLs and cognitive impairment as benefit triggers.
Beneficiary designations often control asset transfer regardless of a will.

Common Traps

Treating Roth contributions as deductible.
Forgetting that traditional retirement distributions are generally ordinary income.
Applying the 10% penalty without checking exceptions.
Treating all 529 distributions as tax-free.
Ignoring whether scholarship funds were used for qualified expenses.
Assuming a will controls assets with beneficiary designations.

Post-2017 NOL carryforwards can generally be carried forward indefinitely.
Starting in 2021, post-2017 NOL carryforwards can offset only 80% of taxable income after pre-2018 NOL carryforwards.
Section 382 limits use of pre-change NOLs after an ownership change.

Section 351 generally makes corporate formation nontaxable when requirements are met.
Transferors must control at least 80% of voting stock and 80% of nonvoting stock immediately after the exchange.
Boot can trigger recognized gain.
Liabilities in excess of basis can trigger gain.
